newsitem.title: USA: United Healthcare says in talks with AARP.
newsitem.headline: United Healthcare says in talks with AARP.

text.p: United HealthCare Corp said on Wednesday it is negotiating to sign a contract with the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) for the delivery of Medicare supplement and hospital indemnity health insurance products.
It said it expects the contract to be considered by the AARP board of directors in November and, if approved, would be effective in January 1998.
The AARP contract currently represents about $4.5 billion in annual premiums and serves 5.7 million persons, it said.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Prudential Insurance Co of America lost its exclusive contract with the AARP, which it has held since 1981 and will still hold until 1997.
The newspaper reported that Metropolitan Life Insurance Co and ITT Hartford Group were also bidding for the contract.
